thoughts.label: Start with Statistics
thoughts.text: Statistics is the exam I fear most, so it gets the first two weeks.
thoughts.prompt: Which exam do you start with, and why?

thoughts.label: Past papers first
thoughts.text: Do three past papers before rereading notes; the gaps show up faster that way.
thoughts.prompt: What comes before rereading notes?

thoughts.label: Fear is uncertainty
thoughts.text: The dread isn't the exam itself; it's not knowing what I don't know yet.
thoughts.prompt: What is the exam dread really about?

thoughts.label: Ninety-minute blocks
thoughts.text: Study in 90-minute blocks with a real break, not endless half-focused hours.
thoughts.prompt: How long is one study block?

thoughts.label: Drop the elective?
thoughts.text: Is the extra elective worth the stress, or should I drop it this term?
thoughts.prompt: What were you unsure about with the elective?

thoughts.label: Teach it back
thoughts.text: Explaining a topic out loud shows what I actually understand.
thoughts.prompt: How do you check you really understand something?

thoughts.label: Ask for an extension
thoughts.text: Email about the project deadline now, not the night before it is due.
thoughts.prompt: What will you ask for, and when?

thoughts.label: Call home Sundays
thoughts.text: A fixed Sunday call means fewer guilty calls in between.
thoughts.prompt: When do you call home?

thoughts.label: Skip the wedding trip?
thoughts.text: Can I say no to the family wedding trip during exams without upsetting everyone?
thoughts.prompt: What were you unsure about saying no to?

thoughts.label: They worry too
thoughts.text: Family asks about jobs because they worry, not to judge me.
thoughts.prompt: Why does family keep asking about jobs?

thoughts.label: Share the plan once
thoughts.text: Tell them the exam and job plan once, clearly, so the questions calm down.
thoughts.prompt: How will you calm the family's questions?

thoughts.label: Home is a reset
thoughts.text: A weekend at home resets me more than another weekend of cramming.
thoughts.prompt: What resets you best?

thoughts.label: Move back home?
thoughts.text: Should I move back home after graduating to save on rent?
thoughts.prompt: Which housing choice is still open?

thoughts.label: Say it early
thoughts.text: Tell one person at home when it's getting too much, before it builds up.
thoughts.prompt: What will you do when it gets too much?

thoughts.label: Three applications weekly
thoughts.text: Three good applications a week beats twenty rushed ones.
thoughts.prompt: How many applications a week?

thoughts.label: Projects beat grades
thoughts.text: Recruiters asked about my projects, never about my grades.
thoughts.prompt: What did recruiters actually ask about?

thoughts.label: Gap year okay?
thoughts.text: Would a gap year look like drifting, or like a choice I can explain?
thoughts.prompt: What was the gap-year worry?

thoughts.label: Apply after exams
thoughts.text: Keep applications light until exams end, then go all in.
thoughts.prompt: When does the big job push start?

thoughts.label: Silence isn't rejection
thoughts.text: Most applications get no reply; silence is not a verdict on me.
thoughts.prompt: What does no reply really mean?

thoughts.label: One page CV
thoughts.text: Cut the CV to one page with three project bullets.
thoughts.prompt: What shape is the CV now?

thoughts.label: Masters or work?
thoughts.text: Is a master's worth the debt, or should I work first and decide later?
thoughts.prompt: Which choice is still open after graduation?

thoughts.label: Rent due the 5th
thoughts.text: Rent leaves on the 5th; move it across the day the stipend lands.
thoughts.prompt: When does rent go out, and what do you do first?

thoughts.label: Cancel two subscriptions
thoughts.text: Cancel the two streaming subscriptions I haven't opened in a month.
thoughts.prompt: What will you cancel?

thoughts.label: Small leaks add up
thoughts.text: Takeaway coffee and snacks cost more each month than my phone bill.
thoughts.prompt: Where is money quietly leaking?

thoughts.label: Part-time job now?
thoughts.text: Can I take weekend shifts without hurting exam prep?
thoughts.prompt: What were you weighing about part-time work?

thoughts.label: Sunday money check
thoughts.text: Ten minutes every Sunday looking at the account, instead of avoiding it.
thoughts.prompt: When do you check your money?

thoughts.label: Avoiding it costs more
thoughts.text: Not looking at the balance made the worry bigger, not smaller.
thoughts.prompt: What made the money worry worse?

thoughts.label: Small buffer first
thoughts.text: Save a small emergency buffer before anything else, even a little each month.
thoughts.prompt: What do you save for first?

thoughts.label: Phone out by 11
thoughts.text: The phone charges outside the room at 11 so I stop scrolling in bed.
thoughts.prompt: What happens at 11 every night?

thoughts.label: Tired makes worries louder
thoughts.text: On short sleep every worry feels twice as big.
thoughts.prompt: What does short sleep do to your worries?

thoughts.label: Walk after lunch
thoughts.text: A twenty-minute walk after lunch clears the afternoon slump.
thoughts.prompt: What clears the afternoon slump?

thoughts.label: Why wake at 4?
thoughts.text: Why do I keep waking at 4 a.m. with my mind racing?
thoughts.prompt: What keeps waking you up?

thoughts.label: Write worries down
thoughts.text: Before bed, put every open thought on paper so my head can let go.
thoughts.prompt: What do you do before bed?

thoughts.label: No coffee after 3
thoughts.text: Coffee after 3 p.m. shows up later as a bad night.
thoughts.prompt: When does coffee start hurting your sleep?

thoughts.label: Cook twice a week
thoughts.text: Cook two big meals a week instead of skipping dinner on study days.
thoughts.prompt: How will you eat better during exams?

threads.why: Avoidance and fatigue both amplify anxiety
Coffee cut mirrors small expense habit
Rent timing helps manage finances when moving
Avoidance heightens anxiety, matching uncertainty insight
Writing worries addresses fear of unknown
Both prioritize exam study before job tasks
Phone limit exemplifies small leak reduction
Early outreach reduces stress in both contexts
Home reset and phone limit both reduce distractions
Writing worries and early sharing both relieve stress
